DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION No. 108 s. 2021 AUG 25 2021 VICE MAYOR ERWIN P. CARALIAN Municipality of Gumaca Province of Quezon Dear Vice-Mayor Caralian: This refers to your letter dated 23 February 2021 requesting for legal opinion conceming the operations of the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) under a re-enacted budget and the letter dated 4 March 2021 from DILG Regional Director Ariel O. Iglesia, Region IV-A referring to the Central Office your aforesaid letter. Per your letter, the SB of Gumaca is currently operating under a re-enacted budget pending legislative authorization of the proposed 2021 Annual Budget which was submitted last 15 October 2020. Under such premise, arose the following queries vis-å-vis Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160): 1) Is there a mandate that the Sangguniang Bayan shall conduct series of Committee Hearings relative to the passage of Annual Budget? 2) Can the Sangguniang Bayan passed (sic) a Resolution relative to the concurrence/non-concurrence of the appointment of a Department Head? a. b. What is the required number of the Sangguniang Bayan? Qualified Majority or Simple Majority? What will be the implication stated under Section 443 (d) of the Code which provides that heads of departments and offices shall be appointed by the municipal mayor with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang bayan members, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. The Sangguniang bayan shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission; othetwise, the same shall be deemed confirmed. 3) Under a re-enacted budget, can the Sangguniang Bayan Members conduct Committee/Hearings? Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

As to the first guery., we are of the view that the conduct of series of Committee Hearings relative to the passage of Annual Budget is not mandatory. Section 323 of Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 provides: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed by the sanggunian concemed. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. xxxx" (Emphasis supplied) The first sentence of the aforequoted provision states that if the SB fails to pass an ordinance authorizing the annual budget, it shall continue to hold sessions, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such session. Clearly, what is being required is the continuous conduct of sessions. The word "session" mentioned therein may refer to either regular or special session conducted by the august body and attended by all or at least majority of the members therein sufficient to constitute a quorum. A regular session is that which has been fixed as to the day, time and place through a Resolution passed by the sanggunian concerned on the first day of the session immediately following the election its members [Section 52 (a), Local Government Code of 19911. A special session, on the other hand, refers to that called by the local chief executive (LCE) or by a majority of the members of the sanggunian when public interest so demands [Section 52 (b), Local Government Code of 19911. A session is different from a committee hearing. A committee hearing is that which is conducted by the members of the committee organized pursuant to Section 501 of the Local Government Code of 1991 while a session, as already mentioned, is conducted SECTION 50. Internal Rules of Procedure. - (a) On the first regular session following the election of its members and within ninety (90) days thereafter, the Sanggunian concerned shall adopt or update its existing rules of procedure. (b) The rules of procedure shall provide for the following: (1) The organization of the Sanggunian and the election of its officers as well as the creation of standing committees which shall include, but shall not be limited to, the committees on appropriations, women and family, human rights, youth and sports development, environmental protection, and cooperatives; the general jurisdiction of each committee; and the election of the chairman and members of each committee; xxxx Page 2 of 5

by the members of the sanggunian and attended by all or at least the majority of the members therein sufficient to constitute a quorum. However, while the conduct of committee hearings is not required under the Local Government Code of 1991, if the members of the sanggunian, after meticulously weighing the issues that are tolling them from enacting the Appropriation Ordinance or Annual Budget, deem it necessary to conduct committee hearings, we are of the view that the same may be conducted. As to the second query, may we re-state Section 443 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , thus: SECTION. 443. Officials of the Municipal Government. — xxxx (d) Unless otherwise provided herein, heads of departments and offices shall be appointed by the municipal mayor with the concurrence of the majority of all the Sanggunianq Bayan members, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. The Sangguniang Bayan shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission; otheMise, the same shall be deemed confirmed. xxxx (Emphasis supplied) Based on the foregoing, the appointment of a department head is considered concurred into by the sanggunian if majority of all its members voted for it. Since the total membership of the sanggunian is considered, the vote required therefore for such concurrence is qualified majority. To differentiate, a simple majority only requires the vote of the majority of the members present there being a quorum. As to the implication of the aforequoted Section 443 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , it bears stressing that the Mayor, as the appointing authority enjoys a wide latitude of discretion as to who shall be appointed to a particular position. The exercise of such discretion solely lies with the Mayor. On the other hand, the power given to the sanggunian to concur such appointment of the Mayor is to be construed as an act confirming that the appointee possesses all the minimum qualifications of a Department Head and that he possesses none of the disqualifications under pertinent laws. If the appointee to the Department Head position possesses all the qualifications and none of the disqualifications as mandated under pertinent laws, the sanggunian has no discretion to deny the concurrence since if that would be allowed, we are of the view that the sanggunian will already be encroaching into the appointing prerogative and discretion of the Mayor and in effect is already substituting their discretion in the process to that of the Mayor's. Based on the aforequoted Section 443 (d) of the Local Government Code of 1991 , the sanggunian is required to act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from its submission. The action required from the sanggunian is the adoption ofa Resolution either concurring or not concurring to the appointment of the Department Head. Failure of the sanggunian to adopt a resolution within 15 days from its receipt of the document would render the appointment deemed confirmed by operation of law. In Page 3 of 5

such case, it becomes a presumption of law that such appointment was already confirmed by the Sangguniang Bayan. As to the we suppose that the committee hearings contemplated herein pertain to matters not related to the enactment of the Appropriations Ordinance such as the adoption of a resolution concurring to the appointment of the department head. In this regard, we reply in the negative. The aforequoted Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 is clear that if the sanggunian concerned failed to pass the Appropriations Ordinance, it shall continue to hold sessions until such ordinance is approved and no other business may be taken up durinq sessions. In Bolos vs. Bolos2, the Supreme Court re-stated this rule in statutory construction: "A cardinal rule in statutory construction is that when the law is clear and free from any doubt or ambiguity, there is no room for construction or interpretation. There is only room for application. As the statute is clear, plain, and free from ambiguity, it must be given its literal meaning and applied without attempted interpretation. This is what is known as the plain- meaning rule or verba legis. It is expressed in the maxim, index animi sermo, or "speech is the index of intention." Furthermore, there is the maxim verba legis non est recedendum, or 'from the words of a statute there should be no departure." The rationale for the rule that "no other business may be taken up during (said) sessions" can be found in Section 305 of the Local Government Code, that is, unless and until the Appropriations Ordinance is approved, no money shall be paid out of the local treasury. Therefore, the Appropriations Ordinance is the most important piece of legislation in a local government unit. The prohibition on taking up other businesses during sanggunian sessions is intended to compel the sanggunian members to devote all their attention to the enactment of the Appropriation Ordinance. While earlier on we differentiated sanggunian session from committee hearing and hold the view that they are not the same, one would argue that Section 323 contemplates only sanggunian sessions thereby excluding committee hearings. Therefore, the conduct of committee hearings not related to the enactment of the Appropriations Ordinance is also prohibited since the conduct thereof nonetheless diverts the attention of the sanggunian members to matters other than the enactment of the Appropriations Ordinance. The same situation that Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 wanted to prevent. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. 2 G.R. No. 186400, October 20, 2010. Page Of 5

We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARLO or Local Government DIR. ARIEL IGLESIA Regional Director, DILG-Region IV-A 3/F Andenson Bldg. 1, National Highway Barangay Parian, City of Calamba, Laguna Page 5 of 5
